output.headline: Accepts $25,000 from Schwab Charitable, via Oakland Public Education Fund, for PreK teacher training
output.summary: The district is accepting a $25,000 regrant through the Oakland Public Education Fund, funded by Schwab Charitable. It pays PreK teachers stipends and extended contract hours to attend a 3-day training on supporting multilingual learners, and to lead trainings and coaching for other teachers. The grant period is July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023 and began before this vote.

output.headline: Ends the district's 2022-23 physical therapy contract with STAC Physical Therapy
output.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) the district's termination for convenience of its 2022-2023 services agreement with STAC Physical Therapy Emeryville, Inc., under Section 11.a of that agreement. The text does not give a reason or any dollar amounts.

output.headline: Sets data-protection terms with Viatron Systems for the 1000 Broadway digitization project
output.summary: This data sharing agreement sets the rules for how the district shares data with Viatron Systems, Inc. and how Viatron must protect it. It applies to Viatron's separate General Service Agreement for the Central Office 1000 Broadway Digitalization Project. The text does not list a payment for this agreement itself.

output.headline: Adopts Aspire Lionel Wilson Preparatory Academy's $73,577.96 Measure N carryover plan
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the board adopts Aspire Lionel Wilson Preparatory Academy's 2021-2022 carryover plan and budget of $73,577.96. A carryover plan covers money left over from the 2021-2022 year.

output.headline: Adopts Envision Academy's $117,793.90 Measure N carryover plan and budget
schools: Envision Academy of Arts and Technology
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the board adopts Envision Academy of Arts and Technology's 2021-2022 carryover plan and budget of $117,793.90. A carryover plan covers money left over from the 2021-2022 year.

output.headline: Adopts East Bay Innovation Academy's $16,638.31 Measure N carryover plan and budget
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the board adopts East Bay Innovation Academy's 2021-2022 carryover plan and budget of $16,638.31. A carryover plan covers money left over from the 2021-2022 year.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $3,000 for a monthly artist at Bella Vista Elementary
output.summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will provide a resident artist once a month to support visual art lessons for TK-5th grade students at Bella Vista Elementary School. The agreement runs October 3, 2022 through May 25, 2023 and began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays BLk up to $27,000 for a fashion industry consultant at Oakland Tech's fashion academy
output.summary: BLk will provide a fashion industry consultant to help teach Career Technical Education courses in fashion fundamentals, design history and marketing at the Fashion Art & Design Academy at Oakland Technical High School. The agreement runs September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Buys Finalsite website platform for up to $263,930 through 2025 using another agency's contract
output.summary: The district would pay Active Internet Technologies (Finalsite) to set up district and school websites, including the staff intranet, and to provide the website platform's license, upgrades and support from January 12, 2023 to June 30, 2025. That includes $77,350 in one-time setup fees in 2022-23 and $93,290 per year in licensing and hosting in each of 2023-24 and 2024-25. The district is buying through the Education Technology Joint Powers Authority's existing contract instead of running its own bid.

output.headline: Sets Ralph J. Bunche Academy's Measure N funding at $850 per pupil, up to $51,069.39 for 2023-24
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title begins with "23-0134", which does not match this item's file number (22-2697).
output.summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, the board puts Ralph J. Bunche Academy at the "Full Implementation" level, $850 per pupil, for the 2023-24 school year. The school is listed as off probation. Spending is capped at $51,069.39.

output.headline: Pays Public Works, LLC up to $148,060 to review and recommend changes to central office departments
output.summary: Public Works, LLC, a consulting firm, will provide a team to review each Continuous School Improvement department against the goals in the district's plan and recommend changes to how those departments are set up. The work comes from a request for proposals (RFP #22-127CSI) and runs December 27, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $45,000 to help write Phase 2 of the district's George Floyd school safety plan
output.summary: An independent consultant will attend project design team meetings, track action items, review how other districts improve school safety while keeping a positive school climate, and help write the Phase 2 George Floyd Implementation Plan. The agreement runs October 3, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Wellness Together up to $40,000 for extra mental health support hours for students
output.summary: Wellness Together will assign a mental health consultant for about 50 weeks, adding five hours a week to an existing Blue Sky Initiative contract. The consultant provides individual check-ins, social-emotional skills groups, family engagement, crisis support and classroom presentations. The agreement runs August 27, 2022 through June 1, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Wellness Together up to $23,760 for a therapist at Edna Brewer Middle School
output.summary: Wellness Together will provide a therapist who works one-on-one with students at Edna Brewer Middle School, listening to their academic, emotional, social and behavioral concerns and helping them set goals. The agreement runs November 14, 2022 through May 25, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Radicle Root Collective up to $3,700 to lead a staff resiliency retreat for newcomer support staff
output.summary: Radicle Root Collective LLC will facilitate a 4-hour retreat in Sonoma for staff of the district's Newcomer Wellness Initiative. Participants will explore resiliency and do small- and large-group reflection and body-based exercises. The retreat ran October 26 through 27, 2022. The Board is ratifying it after the fact.

output.headline: Pays One on One Learning up to $21,000 for learning software, training and coaching for 53 students
output.summary: One on One Learning will provide learning software licenses for up to 53 students, staff training on using data to target instruction, and ongoing teacher coaching and data analysis. The agreement ran October 1 through December 30, 2022. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $11,375 to a contract for English language lesson plans and extends it to April 2023
output.summary: This amendment adds $11,375 to an agreement with an independent contractor who writes supplemental lesson plans to support English language development in 8th grade English language arts. The cap rises from $5,500 to $16,875, and the end date moves from October 31, 2022 to April 30, 2023. It adds both money and time. The Board is ratifying it after the fact.

output.headline: Accepts a free Esports and STEAM classroom at McClymonds High School from Our Own Non-Profit
output.summary: Our Own Non-Profit, Inc. will set up a modern Esports and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) classroom at McClymonds High School, with computer and console stations plus stations for app development and digital content creation. The agreement runs November 4, 2022 through June 30, 2023 at no cost to the district. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Buys $492,545.89 of Apple computer equipment for the new Fremont High School without bidding
output.summary: The Board is asked to find that public bidding would be futile for this purchase, which lets the district skip a competitive bid, and to approve a purchase order with Apple for computer equipment for the Fremont High School new construction project. Work is scheduled to begin January 18, 2023 and last until June 30, 2023. It is paid from Measure J building funds.

output.headline: Accepts free Stanford training for staff on supporting students returning from juvenile justice
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The services agreement is labeled 2021-2022, but the stated term begins November 29, 2022.
output.summary: Stanford University will help train district staff to use a research-validated approach for students returning to school from the juvenile justice system, and will provide training slides, scripts, email templates, flyers and online access. A separate data sharing agreement sets how the district sends data to Stanford and how Stanford protects it. Both are at no cost to the district, and the services term runs November 29, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Pays TransformCA up to $49,027.99 to run the Safe Routes to School walking and biking program
output.summary: TransformCA will run the Safe Routes to School program, which promotes pedestrian and biking safety education and events. The work includes recruiting and sustaining school champions, running events such as Walk and Roll to School Day and Bike to School Day, and submitting quarterly evaluations. The agreement runs November 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $13,000 for HERO's organized recess games at Highland Community School
output.summary: This amendment adds $13,000 to the agreement with HERO, raising the cap from $38,000 to $51,000. HERO runs organized recess games and activities for upper grade students five days a week, teaching conflict management, safety, inclusion and fair play. The agreement period is unchanged, August 29, 2022 through May 25, 2023.

output.headline: Pays Mind Growers up to $18,000 for a facilitator for five monthly Adaptive Schools trainings
output.summary: Mind Growers will provide a facilitator for in-person training sessions from 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM once a month for five months, based on the Adaptive Schools Foundation Seminar. The goal is to build collaborative, self-directed thinkers. The agreement runs August 1 through December 31, 2022. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Zymbolic LLC up to $8,400 for social-emotional learning support at Oakland Technical High
output.summary: Zymbolic LLC will provide school-wide social-emotional learning support for educators and students at Oakland Technical High School, using lessons, games, restorative justice community-building circles and role-playing activities. The agreement runs November 1, 2022 through May 31, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $15,000 to draft Proposition 39 facility offers for charter schools
output.summary: A San Francisco consultant will help the Charter Schools Office prepare the district's preliminary Proposition 39 facilities offer, including classroom entitlement calculations, the offer letter and exhibits. It runs November 7, 2022 to February 28, 2023, for up to $15,000. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

output.headline: Hires LCA Architects for up to $88,160 to close out old state-review building projects
output.summary: A new agreement with LCA Architects for design and engineering services to finish the paperwork on outstanding older projects that still need certification from the Division of the State Architect. The limit is $88,160.00: $75,600.00 for basic services, $7,560.00 for additional services and $5,000.00 for reimbursable expenses. Work runs from January 12, 2023 to December 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays Rigorous Love up to $6,000 for nine anti-racism workshops for LIFE Academy staff and parents
output.summary: Rigorous Love will offer nine workshops or trainings for all staff and parents at LIFE Academy on building an anti-racist school community. The agreement runs January 3 through January 31, 2023. The Board is ratifying it, and the service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays a culture keeper up to $48,000 to support African American girls at West Oakland Middle School
output.summary: The district hired an individual contractor to work each day from 9 to 4 as a culture keeper and facilitator for African American girls' groups. The work includes helping students with issues, running mediations and in-house suspensions, supervising lunchtime, and coaching new teachers on classroom management. The agreement runs September 27, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays Attitudinal Healing Connection up to $23,750 for visual arts programs at Allendale Elementary
output.summary: Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc will provide its ArtEsteem visual arts programming and after-school visual arts classes at Allendale Elementary School. The agreement runs November 14, 2022 through May 25, 2023. The Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays Carter-Kelly Consulting/Lifepoint up to $7,000 to coordinate student support at Dewey Academy
output.summary: Carter-Kelly Consulting/Lifepoint will provide 65 hours of services to help Dewey Academy students overcome barriers to meeting graduation requirements. The contractor will also serve as the school's Student Success Team Coordinator. The agreement runs December 1, 2022 through May 26, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Awards G & G Builders up to $83,995 to prepare the Centro Infantil play area for new matting and equipment
output.summary: G & G Builders was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder for the site preparation needed before play matting and a play structure are installed at the Centro Infantil Child Development Center. The limit of $83,995 includes a $13,000 contingency allowance (extra money set aside for unexpected costs). Work is expected to start January 23, 2023 and last 30 days, ending around February 21, 2023.

output.headline: Accepts My Other Brother's no-cost student mentoring and support program at Castlemont High School
output.summary: My Other Brother will work with teachers and staff to hold weekly individual and group meetings that give Castlemont High School students academic and social-emotional support, tutoring, and an after-school football study hall. The program also builds leadership, life skills and youth research opportunities. It runs September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023 at no cost to the district, and the Board is approving it after the start date (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays My Other Brother up to $20,000 for an after-school program for Black boys at Hoover Elementary
output.summary: My Other Brother will serve 4th and 5th grade Black male students at Hoover Elementary School. Students meet after school on Mondays and Wednesdays for community building, workshops on identity and leadership, and a youth-led research project. The agreement runs November 1, 2022 through May 25, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Accepts My Other Brother's no-cost college mentoring for Black youth at Dewey Academy
output.summary: My Other Brother will bring college-age Black men and women to mentor Black youth at Dewey Academy through mentorship, workshops and cultural dialogue sessions. The goal is to strengthen the pipeline to college and build students' sense of belonging. It runs October 3, 2022 through May 25, 2023 at no cost to the district, and the Board is approving it after the start date (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays Junior Center of Art and Science up to $23,100 for a contemporary art program at Emerson Elementary
output.summary: Junior Center of Art and Science will introduce Emerson Elementary School students to contemporary artists and their work. Students learn about visual representation, art history, and how artists give voice to big ideas that affect their communities. The agreement runs September 12, 2022 through May 25, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays Attitudinal Healing Connection up to $25,000 to coordinate an arts grant program at Bret Harte Middle
output.summary: Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc will provide a consultant to work with the school on planning and outreach for the Art Incentive Grant (AIG) 2025 Program. The consultant will tell students, families and staff about the program and help with site-based planning and evaluation. The agreement runs October 10, 2022 through May 31, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $85,200 for six AmeriCorps staff at Oakland International High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will provide six AmeriCorps staff members to support instruction and learning in classes, the after-school program and across Oakland International High School. The agreement runs November 1, 2022 through May 25, 2023.

output.summary: This amendment adds more student safety intervention and social-emotional support and case management for students who are not newcomers and were affected by COVID-19 school closures. It raises the maximum from $60,000 to $180,000 for the period August 15, 2022 through May 26, 2023. All other terms stay the same.

output.summary: SmoothSynsations will act as a fashion industry mentor for Career Technical Education courses in fashion design, fashion history and fashion marketing at Oakland Technical High School. The work includes developing a pilot student-run business and student projects using industry equipment. The agreement runs September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.summary: Tandem, Partners in Early Learning will provide workshops for families and educators on trauma-informed practices and social-emotional development. The work is for the Early Childhood Development Department from November 14, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.summary: The Speech Pathology Group, doing business as SPG Therapy & Education, will provide monthly professional development to staff in the district's elementary, middle and high school expanded learning (after-school) programs. The agreement runs December 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.summary: Adds a final walkthrough, inspection and follow-up training for the newly installed refrigeration system at The Center Project. output.summary: Rigorous Love will lead 9 workshops or trainings for all staff on building an anti-racist school community and trauma-informed classrooms. output.summary: ACC Environmental Consultants will check that abatement (removal of hazardous materials) rules are followed, observe worker safety procedures, keep a daily log of the contractor's activities and write reports for the 2111 International Fire Alarm Project. output.summary: Higher Ground Neighborhood Development Corp will provide in-class support, gender-specific behavioral skill-building groups, general supervision, contract staffing and preventive mentoring at East Oakland Pride Elementary School, as described in the agreement's Exhibit A. The agreement runs August 8, 2022 through May 25, 2023.

output.headline: Pays Community Development Finance up to $25,200 to distribute student stipends for academic recovery
output.summary: Community Development Finance will distribute stipends to students, as directed by the Assistant Principal of the Central Academic Recovery Team. The stipends reward satisfactory presence, participation and contribution in work-based learning activities and in a 9th and 10th grade summer academic recovery program. The agreement runs December 5, 2022 through June 30, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $99,000 for after-school video and animation classes for high schoolers
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will teach after-school classes in video production, filmmaking and animation, open to any district high school student. Animation classes meet Monday and Wednesday and video production classes meet Tuesday and Thursday. The agreement runs January 12, 2023 through May 24, 2023.

output.headline: Pays FEV Tutor up to $29,000 for academic success coaches and approves a student data sharing agreement
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The funding source is listed as "No Fiscal Impact" even though the text authorizes a cost of up to $29,000.00.
output.summary: Focus Care Inc, doing business as FEV Tutor Inc, will provide Academic Success Coaches to give students academic support from December 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is also approving a data sharing agreement (DSA) that sets the rules for how the district shares student data with FEV Tutor and how the company must protect it.

vendor.name: Focus Care Inc dba FEV Tutor Inc

output.headline: Pays Banteay Srei Asian Health Services up to $36,000 for workshops for Southeast Asian young women
output.summary: Banteay Srei Asian Health Services will host weekly workshops for Southeast Asian young women to build leadership, peer support networks and family support. The workshops also teach about women's health and sexual assault. The agreement runs December 12, 2022 through May 25, 2023, and the Board is approving it after the work began (a ratification).

output.headline: Pays a youth engagement consultant up to $99,100 to build student leadership in expanded learning programs
output.summary: An individual contractor will build youth engagement and restorative justice leadership into the district's expanded learning (after-school) programs. The work includes running trainings and partnership meetings, recruiting and preparing youth for internships, and piloting a middle school youth leadership program. The agreement runs January 12, 2023 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $99,100 to build youth leadership in Expanded Learning programs
output.summary: The district hires an Oakland consultant to build systems for student engagement and restorative justice leadership in its Expanded Learning programs, from elementary through high school. The work includes training for youth and adults, preparing students for internships, and starting a middle school youth leadership program. It runs January 12 to June 30, 2023, for up to $99,100.

output.headline: Approves free garden, food and tree programs from Growing Together - Bay Area at Oakland schools
output.summary: Growing Together - Bay Area will provide garden and nutrition education, fruit and vegetable distribution, tree education and site stewardship at several schools, plus programming at Castlemont High School, at no cost to the district. It runs December 2, 2022 to June 30, 2023. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

output.headline: Pays Growing Together - Bay Area up to $15,000 for farm and garden education at Castlemont High
output.summary: Growing Together - Bay Area will give Castlemont High School students farm and garden stewardship and education, plus training in fresh food enterprises, logistics and operations. It runs December 19, 2022 to June 30, 2023, for up to $15,000. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

output.headline: Lets the Superintendent warn administrators of possible reassignment or release for 2023-24
output.summary: This authorizes the Superintendent or a designee to send notices to administrative and supervisory certificated (credentialed) employees that they could be reassigned or released from their current positions for the 2023-2024 school year. The notice is sent under California Education Code Section 44951. The text names no specific employees or dollar amounts.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $19,000 for organized recess games at Bella Vista Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run 25 hours a week of organized recess games and physical activity at Bella Vista Elementary School. The sessions teach students problem solving, conflict management and teamwork. It runs January 3 to May 25, 2023, for up to $19,000.

output.headline: Lets the Superintendent send release notices to probationary and temporary teachers not rehired for 2023-24
output.summary: This authorizes the Superintendent or a designee to send a notice of release to each probationary and temporary certificated (credentialed) employee who will not be re-elected for the 2023-2024 school year. It follows California Education Code Sections 44929.21 and 44954. The text names no specific employees or dollar amounts.

output.headline: Lets the Superintendent warn grant-funded teachers of possible reassignment for 2023-24
output.summary: This authorizes the Superintendent or a designee to send a notice of possible reassignment for the 2023-2024 school year to all categorically funded certificated (credentialed) employees. Categorically funded positions are paid from specific funding sources. The notice follows California Education Code Section 44909, and the text names no specific employees or dollar amounts.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $44,000 to staff four Family Champions at Urban Promise Academy
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will act as fiscal sponsor, meaning it contracts and pays four part-time Family Champions. They help supervise students walking to and from school and during recess and lunch, and do family outreach with the Family Resource Center staff, to improve student safety at Urban Promise Academy. It runs January 1 to May 30, 2023, for up to $44,000.

output.headline: Pays Freedom Soul Media Education up to $90,000 for staff workshops on racial slurs and hate
output.summary: Freedom Soul Media Education will lead workshops for staff and administrators on intersecting forms of oppression and on the harm caused by the N-word, racial slurs and hate. The district's Office of Equity oversees the work. It runs November 1, 2022 to May 31, 2023, for up to $90,000. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

output.headline: Adds $23,500 to Quetzal Education Consulting's anti-racism training contract, raising it to $42,000
output.summary: This amendment adds $23,500 to the district's agreement with Quetzal Education Consulting for its Disrupting Anti-Blackness professional development, toolkit resources and leaders sessions, raising the limit from $18,500 to $42,000. The Office of Equity oversees the work, which runs October 3, 2022 to May 3, 2023. The board is ratifying the amendment after the service period began.

output.headline: Approves free English language development coaching from Alameda County Office of Education
output.summary: The Alameda County Office of Education will provide professional development and leadership support to help the district put designated English Language Development (ELD) into practice, at no cost to the district. It runs January 3 to June 30, 2023, and is managed by the English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department. The board is ratifying the agreement.

output.headline: Hires Lozano Smith law firm for up to $50,000 in legal help for Nutrition Services
output.summary: Lozano Smith will give the Nutrition Services Department legal advice as needed under a memorandum of understanding (a written agreement) and engagement policy. The limit is $50,000 in a fiscal year, and the period runs October 17, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Curriculum Associates up to $107,017.50 for implementation services and staff training at 11 schools
output.summary: Curriculum Associates, LLC will provide initial implementation services, account management, staff development consultation and resources, and technical support for 11 named middle and high schools. The Academics and Instruction Department oversees it. The service period runs August 11, 2022 to June 30, 2023, for up to $107,017.50, and began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves McCormick Barstow law firm for legal work, up to $99,100 a year, through June 2025
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding and engagement policy lets the district's Legal Department hire McCormick Barstow, through letters of engagement, for legal advice, counsel and defense, including claims and civil lawsuits, as needed. Total letters of engagement are capped at $99,100 in each fiscal year. It runs November 1, 2022 to June 30, 2025, and the board is ratifying it.

output.headline: Pays Stronger Consulting up to $13,000 to review hiring and recruit staff for the Charter Schools Office
output.summary: Stronger Consulting, Inc. will evaluate the current hiring process and recommend changes to improve retention. It will also recruit candidates to fill a current vacancy. The Charter Schools Office oversees the work, which runs December 5, 2022 to January 31, 2023, for up to $13,000. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $44,000 Packard Foundation grant for kindergarten teachers to use the Early Development Instrument
output.summary: The district accepts $44,000 from the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, passed through the Oakland Public Education Fund, to help OUSD kindergarten teachers carry out the Early Development Instrument. The grant period is September 30, 2022 to June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital Oakland up to $99,000 for early childhood mental health services
output.summary: The hospital will provide mental health services to young children and families, including individual and small group therapy, family treatment, parent workshops and assessments. It will also train educators to understand child development and the stress children and families face. The Early Childhood Education Department oversees it. It runs November 30, 2022 to June 30, 2023, for up to $99,000. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

vendor.name: Children's Hospital & Research Center at Oakland dba UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital Oakland

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $38,000 for organized recess games and coaching at Oakland Academy of Knowledge
output.summary: HERO will run organized recess games and physical activity, and offer its Young HERO Program to upper-grade students five days a week. Coaches will lead safe games and teach conflict management, safety, inclusion, responsibility and fair play. It runs January 4 to May 25, 2023, at Oakland Academy of Knowledge, for up to $38,000.

output.headline: Pays Children Rising up to $5,000 for tutoring at Horace Mann Elementary
output.summary: Children Rising will run a tutoring program at Horace Mann Elementary School for students the school identifies as needing it through its intervention planning. It runs October 10, 2022 to May 19, 2023, for up to $5,000. The board is ratifying the agreement, which began before the vote.

output.headline: Pays Destiny Arts Center up to $27,000 for drumming and movement classes at Bella Vista Elementary
output.summary: Destiny Arts Center will teach drumming and movement classes to students at Bella Vista Elementary School. It runs January 3 to June 30, 2023, for up to $27,000.

output.headline: Pays Spearitwurx up to $100,000 for anti-racist training and wellness kits for district staff
output.summary: Spearitwurx will provide anti-racist professional development and wellness kits for all OUSD teachers and staff. The Office of Equity oversees the work. The service period runs September 1, 2022 to May 31, 2023, for up to $100,000, and began before the board vote.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $8,660 for YouthBeats video work at Oakland International High
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will provide students with spring work alongside YouthBeats staff, connected to their Career Technical Education class on video production at Oakland International High School. It runs January 3 to April 30, 2023, for up to $8,660.

output.headline: Accepts $50,000 from the Helzel Family Foundation Fund for high school literacy at Life Academy
output.summary: The district accepts a $50,000 grant from The Helzel Family Foundation Fund at The East Bay Community Foundation, on behalf of Life Academy, for high school literacy instruction. The grant period is January 1 to December 31, 2023.

vendor.name: The Helzel Family Foundation Fund at The East Bay Community Foundation

output.headline: Approves the December 14, 2022 regular Board of Education meeting minutes
output.summary: The board ratifies the written minutes of its regular meeting on December 14, 2022. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. No money is involved.

output.headline: Approves the January 4, 2023 special Board of Education meeting minutes
output.summary: The board ratifies the written minutes of its special meeting on January 4, 2023. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. No money is involved.
